title: Usage fairness: soft-burst windows, prorated entitlements, & overage reconciliation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a predictable soft-burst mechanism and prorated entitlement reconciliation for plan tiers, plus billing acceptance criteria and backend reconciliation rules to ensure fair usage and transparent overage charges.
background: Customers have asked for temporary burst capacity beyond quota for short spikes without immediate throttling or opaque overage hooks. Current system either throttles immediately or bills at flat overage rates, leading to customer confusion and support tickets. The goal is to enable short soft-burst windows that allow short-lived spikes, automatically prorate monthly entitlements when plan changes occur mid-cycle, and add deterministic reconciliation logic that produces human-readable billing line items.
goals: Allow short-duration soft bursts (configurable window) before applying strict quota enforcement
Automatically prorate entitlements when customers upgrade/downgrade mid-billing-cycle
Ensure overage billing is deterministic and itemized in invoices (burst vs sustained overage)
Reduce support tickets related to unexpected throttles or opaque charges by 50% within 2 months of launch
non_functional_requirements: Burst evaluation must add <5ms median latency to request routing path
Quota checks and billing events must be idempotent and replay-safe
Reconciliation job should complete within 4 hours for >95% of accounts
All changes must be backward compatible for existing entitlements and not alter past invoices
in_scope: API/console controls for configuring soft-burst window and capacity per plan
Billing reconciliation rules and invoice line item generation for burst vs sustained usage
Proration algorithm for partial-cycle plan changes
Acceptance criteria and test harnesses for billing edge cases
Docs and console copy explaining burst behavior and proration
out_of_scope: Changing core rate limits or token pricing for plans
Per-token cost-optimization recommendations (handled by Optimize team)
Introducing new plan SKUs (this PRD adjusts handling only)
requirements: REQ-1: Soft-burst window: allow configurable N-second window where usage above quota is recorded as 'burst' and not immediately billed as overage
REQ-2: Burst quota cap: burst usage is allowed up to a percentage of monthly quota (configurable per plan, default 20%) within the window
REQ-3: Sustained usage threshold: if sustained usage beyond quota persists for M consecutive minutes (configurable), mark as sustained and subject to overage pricing or throttling
REQ-4: Proration on change: when plan is changed mid-cycle, recalc entitled units for each day and prorate unused units into credits or additional charges
REQ-5: Invoice clarity: generate separate invoice lines for 'burst allowance', 'sustained overage', and 'proration adjustments' with human-readable metadata and links to usage dashboard
REQ-6: Admin controls: Console and API endpoints to set plan-level default burst window and override per-customer
REQ-7: Auditability: all burst/grace decisions must emit events to audit-log and be queryable in Console for 13 months
user_stories: As a growth-stage customer I want brief traffic spikes to be absorbed by a soft-burst window so my frontend doesn't degrade during short load bursts
As an account owner I want to see a clear invoice breakdown showing proration and burst charges so I can reconcile cost with usage
As a billing ops engineer I want deterministic reconciliation output so refunds/credits can be automated and audited
As a PM I want console defaults but the ability to override burst window per-customer for enterprise accounts
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Launch config exposes plan-level 'burst_window_seconds' and 'burst_cap_percent' with sane defaults (default 300s, 20%)
AC-2: In test harness, a simulated spike that fits within burst window and cap does not trigger overage billing and is recorded as 'burst' in usage logs
AC-3: If spike extends past the sustained threshold, system marks the interval as 'sustained' and billing events apply overage rates starting at sustained boundary

AC-4: Mid-cycle upgrade from Plan A to Plan B produces a proration line item equal to (days_remaining / days_in_cycle) * (new_plan_units - old_plan_units) and appears on invoice with explanatory metadata
AC-5: Reconciliation job produces the same invoice entries when run twice (idempotent) and emits event with reconciliation_id visible in console
AC-6: Console shows per-customer burst usage graph and link to invoice lines for 13-month retention
AC-7: End-to-end tests for 10 synthetic customer profiles validate expected invoice totals within 0.5% of spec
billing_acceptance_criteria: BAC-1: Overage classification must be stable: any usage marked as 'burst' on ingestion cannot be reclassified to 'sustained' retroactively except through a flagged reconciliation run with human approval
BAC-2: All invoice line items required by AC-4 are included and match reconciliation CSV exports used by finance
BAC-3: Proration credits are applied to next invoice if billing cycle is already invoiced; finance receives CSV of unapplied credits
BAC-4: Support-facing billing timeline (event stream) shows exact timestamps and reasoning for each billed event for at least 13 months
BAC-5: Billing integration tests with third-party invoicing system validate that line item metadata is preserved and displayed correctly
edge_cases: Large sustained spike that alternates between allowed burst and sustained thresholds due to interleaved short drops — reconcile into contiguous sustained intervals for billing
Customer downgrades to a lower plan mid-cycle and then spikes — proration must not double-count burst allowance from previous higher plan
Clock drift across ingest nodes — use reconciliation job to normalize boundaries using canonical billing timestamps
Manual adjustments by support — any manual crediting must annotate original reconciliation_id and retain immutability of original events
metrics_and_kpis: Reduction in billing-support tickets related to unexpected throttles/charges: target 50% decrease within 60 days
Percentage of accounts where burst usage prevented immediate throttling during measured spike events: target 95% for spikes < burst_window
Invoice generation latency: 99th percentile < 6 hours after reconciliation completes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): enable soft-burst for 50 internal accounts and finance/sales shadow invoices (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (early customers): rollout to 200 opt-in customers with visibility controls and dedicated support channel (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (general availability): enable by default for all new billing cycles, existing customers opt-in, monitor metrics and rollback safety in place (1 week)
Rollback plan: toggle per-account burst_window_seconds=0 to immediately disable burst behavior and rerun reconciliation for affected accounts
dependencies: ENG-3412: Quota evaluation service - add burst label to usage records
ENG-3520: Billing reconciliation worker - support itemized invoice lines
ENG-3567: Console UI - add burst config and graphs
Finance: CSV ingestion schema update and mapping
open_questions: Q1: Default values: should burst_window_seconds default to 300s or 600s? (ops prefers 300s, growth suggests 600s)
Q2: Should burst cap percent be absolute of monthly quota or scaled by recent 30-day baseline?
Q3: For enterprise customers, do we offer unlimited burst behind a rate-limited 'sustained' fallback?
Q4: What is the support process for contested reconciliations (customer disputes)?
decisions: D1: Default burst_window_seconds=300 and burst_cap_percent=20 agreed by PM/Finance after 2026-02-15 sync
D2: Reconciliation must be idempotent and produce reconciliation_id for traceability
D3: Retroactive reclassification of burst -> sustained requires human approval logged in support workflow
testing_plan: Unit tests for burst classifier logic with synthetic timelines
Integration tests: end-to-end billing run against staging data and ledger exports
Chaos test: simulate ingest node clock skew and verify reconciliation normalizes boundaries
Acceptance tests: finance verifies 10 weeks of historical scenarios match expected invoices
docs_and_ux: Console copy: short explainer on plan page and billing page describing burst behavior
Billing FAQ entry with examples and sample invoice screenshots
Developer docs: API fields, event schemas, and reconciliation run API
